# STRIKE-Q1 — Melt-Up Signal Census · RESULTS

**Run date:** 2026-08-17 · **Lane:** STRIKE · **Executor:** Claude Code (Codex brief `docs/codex-briefs/2026-08-17-strike-filing-batch-brief.md`)
**Source query file:** `docs/strike/queries/STRIKE-Q1-melt-up-census.sql`

This file is **descriptive only**. Raw outputs, row counts, the Rosetta mapping and a
list of observations. No outcome grades, no expectancy, no edge claims, no fixes and
no interpretation — interpretation is STRIKE's job. `signal_outcomes` was not queried.

## Windows (UTC, half-open `[start, end)`)

| Window | Range |
|---|---|
| CORE (melt-up) | `2026-07-30T00:00Z` → `2026-08-05T00:00Z` |
| Q1a (trip window) | `2026-08-05T00:00Z` → `2026-08-16T00:00Z` |

## Protocol compliance

| Rule | How it was honoured |
|---|---|
| SELECT-only, no DDL/DML/temp tables | Connection opened with `set_session(readonly=True)`; the server itself would reject any write. Only `SET TIME ZONE` / `SHOW` ran alongside the filed statements. |
| Execute in order, Q0 first as a gate | Q0.1 and Q0.2 were run and evaluated **before** any other statement was executed. |
| No query rewriting | Every statement below is reproduced verbatim from the `.sql` file and was executed exactly as filed. |
| Errors returned unedited | No statement raised. Nothing was suppressed. |
| Timestamps computed in-DB in UTC; never re-rendered client-side | Session TZ pinned to `UTC`, and psycopg2's typecasters were replaced with passthroughs for every date / time / numeric / array OID, so all values are the **server's own text**. No Python `datetime` or `Decimal` repr appears anywhere in this file. |
| `COUNT(*)` only, no planner estimates | All counts are `COUNT(*)` from the filed statements. |

## Gate determination (Q0)

**Column gate — PASS.** Q0.1 confirms `signals` carries `created_at`, `status`, `score`,
`ticker` and `strategy`, and `unified_positions` carries `ticker`. The explicit stop
condition in the file — *"If `strategy` is not a signals column (e.g. it is
`strategy_name` or `signal_type`), STOP"* — does **not** trigger: `strategy` is a real
`character varying` column on `signals` (`signal_type` also exists, separately).
Therefore **Q1–Q5, Q9 and Q1a were cleared to run.**

**Name gates — Q6, Q7 and Q8 all STOP.** None of the three target tables exists.
Nothing was substituted and no query was rewritten; details in *Gated queries* below.

| Query | Target table | Present in Q0.2? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q6 | `webhook_events` | No — but `pythia_events` is | **NOT RUN** (name differs; file says note it, don't run) |
| Q7 | `b2_options_shadow` | No — no `%b2%` / `%resolver%` table at all | **NOT RUN** |
| Q8 | `hydra_scores` | No — no `%hydra%` hit at all | **NOT RUN** |

Per the brief, the name-gate failures stop **those queries**, not the census; the
column gate that would have stopped everything passed.

## Q3 — CORE census: semis/AI subset, daily counts + score stats

SQL executed verbatim (statement 5 of 17):

```sql
SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS utc_day,
       COUNT(*) AS n,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE score >= 65) AS n_ge65,
       MAX(score) AS max_score
FROM signals
WHERE created_at >= '2026-07-30T00:00:00Z'
  AND created_at <  '2026-08-05T00:00:00Z'
  AND ticker IN ('NVDA','AMD','AVGO','MRVL','ARM','INTC','MU','TSM','SMCI',
                 'ALAB','CRDO','ANET','VRT','WOLF','ENTG','LRCX','AMAT',
                 'QCOM','LSCC','MXL','UMC','ON','KLAC','COHR','AAOI','FN',
                 'SOXL','SOXS','SMH','SOXX','QQQ')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

       status,

WHERE created_at >= '2026-07-30T00:00:00Z'

# Rosetta — label → codename mapping

Appended verbatim from `backend/config/strategy_aliases.py` (read at run time,
2026-08-17). Reproduced exactly as it appears in the file; no edits.

```python
# signal_type (UPPER) → codename. Most specific; checked first.
CODENAME_BY_SIGNAL_TYPE: Dict[str, str] = {
    "GOLDEN_TOUCH": "Midas",
    "TRAPPED_SHORTS": "Hector",
    "APIS_CALL": "Apis",
    "KODIAK_CALL": "Kodiak",
    # Achilles family — also covered by the strategy map, listed here so a row
    # carrying only signal_type still resolves.
    "SELL_RIP_EMA": "Achilles",
    "SELL_RIP_VWAP": "Achilles",
    "SELL_RIP_EARLY": "Achilles",
    # L2 (pre-mapped, ready for emit)
    "NEMESIS_LONG": "Nemesis",
    "NEMESIS_SHORT": "Nemesis",
    "WHALE_LONG": "Triton",
    "WHALE_SHORT": "Triton",
    "WHALE_BULLISH": "Triton",
    "WHALE_BEARISH": "Triton",
}

# strategy (lower) → codename. Checked after signal_type. Covers families where
# one strategy spans several signal_types.
CODENAME_BY_STRATEGY: Dict[str, str] = {
    "sell_the_rip": "Achilles",
    "whale_hunter": "Triton",
    "nemesis": "Nemesis",
    "nemesis_wrr": "Nemesis",
}
```

Resolution precedence, verbatim from the same file's docstring:

```
Precedence (codename()):
  1. signal_type-keyed match (most specific)
  2. strategy-keyed match (covers multi-signal_type families, e.g. all
     SELL_RIP_* under strategy `sell_the_rip` → Achilles)
  3. unmapped → None  (callers fall back to the existing display formatting;
     returning None — not the raw string — is deliberate so the frontend's
     `signal.codename || formatSignalType(...)` prefer-pattern degrades to the
     richer JS formatter instead of surfacing a raw UPPER_SNAKE value)
```

```
NOTE — Icarus (0DTE SPY scalp) has no discoverable underlying signal_type /
strategy identifier in the codebase as of 2026-06-17; it is intentionally left
unmapped (falls through to display_name's humanized fallback) until its
identifier is confirmed. L2 names (Triton/Nemesis) are pre-mapped so they are
ready when those strategies emit.
```

# Anomalies observed

Observations only. No fixes, no interpretation, no severity assigned.

1. **Rosetta covers 1 of the 6 live strategy labels.** Of the six distinct raw
   `strategy` values in the two windows, only `sell_the_rip` resolves through
   `strategy_aliases.py` (→ Achilles). The other five return `codename() = None`,
   including the two highest-volume labels: `Holy_Grail` (199 rows CORE, 411 trip)
   and `Artemis` (149 CORE, 333 trip).

2. **Q0.2's `%mp_%` pattern behaved as a wildcard, not a literal.** In `ILIKE`,
   `_` matches any single character, so `%mp_%` matched `bias_composite_history`
   ("co**mpo**site") and `close_attempts` ("atte**mpt**s") rather than only
   `mp_`-prefixed market-profile tables. Those two names are in Q0.2's output for
   that reason. Cross-checking each returned name against the patterns: the eight
   hits resolve to `%pythia%` (1), `%options%` (2), `%watch%` (3) and `%mp_%` (2).
   **No name matched `%webhook%`, `%hydra%`, `%b2%`, `%resolver%`,
   `%market_profile%` or `%tag%`** — which is what drives the Q6/Q7/Q8 gates.

3. **`signals.created_at` is `timestamp without time zone`,** but the census filters
   compare it against Zulu-suffixed literals (`'2026-07-30T00:00:00Z'`). Postgres
   parses those as `timestamp without time zone` and silently discards the `Z`
   offset, so the window boundaries are applied against naive values. Separately,
   `date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')` interprets a naive value as
   UTC and returns a `timestamptz`, whose text rendering then depends on the
   session TZ (pinned to UTC for this run).

4. **Mixed timezone-awareness inside `signals`.** Most timestamp columns are
   `timestamp without time zone` (`created_at`, `timestamp`, `expires_at`,
   `enriched_at`, `decided_at`, …) while `outcome_resolved_at` and
   `context_updated_at` are `timestamp with time zone`.

5. **`width_bucket` decile 11 is the overflow bucket, not a 101–110 band.**
   `width_bucket(score, 0, 100, 10)` returns 11 when `score` is exactly 100.
   CORE has 1 such row; the trip window has 34 (32 `COMMITTEE_REVIEW`,
   2 `DISMISSED`). These are `score = 100.00` exactly.

6. **Only three status values appear in either window:** `COMMITTEE_REVIEW`,
   `DISMISSED`, `EXPIRED`. No active, triggered, filled or executed state is
   present in the census output.

7. **No `NULL` scores in either window.** Q5 and Q1a.4 bucket totals (497 and
   1059) reconcile exactly with the Q1 and Q1a.1 status totals, so `width_bucket`
   produced no `NULL` decile.

8. **Calendar gaps align with weekends.** CORE has no rows for 2026-08-01 (Sat) or
   2026-08-02 (Sun); the trip window has none for 2026-08-08 (Sat) or 2026-08-09
   (Sun). **Exception:** 2026-08-15 *is* a Saturday and does carry 12 rows, all
   `EXPIRED`, with no `COMMITTEE_REVIEW` or `DISMISSED`.

9. **`COMMITTEE_REVIEW` is concentrated in one label.** CORE: 54 of 55 review rows
   are `CTA Scanner`, the 55th `Artemis`. Trip: 111 of 116 are `CTA Scanner`, the
   other 5 `Artemis`. `Holy_Grail` — the highest-volume label overall — has **zero**
   `COMMITTEE_REVIEW` rows in either window.

10. **`CTA Scanner` review rows sit above a score floor** (min 73.70 CORE, 71.50
    trip), yet its `DISMISSED` rows reach `max_score = 100.00` in the trip window —
    i.e. a 100-score row was dismissed rather than sent to review.

11. **`Crypto Scanner` appears only in the trip window** (45 `EXPIRED`, scores
    25.00–52.00) and is absent from CORE entirely.

12. **Q9 did not reproduce its stated DEF candidate.** The query is annotated
    *"DEF candidate: negative current_price rendering in unified_positions"*. Across
    all 9 QQQ rows **no `current_price` is negative** — the values are
    `0.0149…`, `0.0749…`, `NULL`, `NULL`, `NULL`, `0.445`, `5.79`, `0.8199…`, `0`.
    Only 9 rows came back against `LIMIT 20`, so this is the complete QQQ set in
    `unified_positions`, not a truncated sample.

13. **`dte` is frozen at entry while price fields are live.** Both OPEN QQQ rows
    (`id` 356 and 355, entry 2026-07-21, expiry 2026-10-16) carry `dte = 87`.
    87 is exactly entry→expiry; today→expiry is 60. Their `price_updated_at` is
    `2026-08-17 20:32Z` — i.e. refreshed the same day this census ran — so `dte`
    and the price fields are on different vintages within the same row.

14. **`numeric` columns carry full float64 expansion artifacts.** e.g.
    `unrealized_pnl = -17.800000000000000710542735760100185871124267578125`,
    `current_price = 0.01499999999999999944488848768742172978818416595458984375`,
    `cost_basis = 55.00000000000000710542735760100185871124267578125`. These are the
    **server's own text** for `numeric` columns, confirmed via passthrough
    typecasters — not a client-side rendering artifact of this run.

15. **Q9's `ORDER BY 1 DESC` orders by `id`,** the surrogate key — so "top 20" is
    newest-by-insertion-id, not by `entry_date` or `created_at`. Row order does not
    follow date order in the output (`id` 320 has an earlier `entry_date` than
    `id` 290's `created_at`).

16. **Q4's payload is dominated by one column.** The 50-row Q4 result is ~838 000
    characters, of which `bias_at_signal` is 617 649 (73.7 %), `triggering_factors`
    87 682 (10.5 %) and `score_v2_factors` 65 820 (7.9 %). This is what drives this
    results file to ~1 MB. Recorded because it affects the file, not the data.

17. **Direction/structure pairing in `unified_positions`.** All `put_debit_spread`
    rows carry `direction = SHORT` and the single `call_debit_spread` row carries
    `direction = LONG`; the one `long_put` row (`id` 320) also carries
    `direction = SHORT`. `legs` is `NULL` on all 9 rows despite the column existing.

18. **Two OPEN QQQ spreads sit far from spot.** `id` 356 is 360/350 (breakeven
    `{359.959…}`) and `id` 355 is 510/500 (breakeven `{509.759…}`), both expiring
    2026-10-16, both `max_profit` ≈ 2977.70 / 2903.70 against `cost_basis` 22.30 /
    96.30. Stated as recorded values only.
